units: <cite ref="Shabbat 104b:9">Sabb. 104ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ היא אלא וכ׳</he> it is a writing, and what is needed to make it one word is bringing the two ends of the papers close together.
<cite ref="Menachot 34a:13">Men. 34ᵃ</cite> <he>כ׳ הנוהגת לדורות</he> a mode of writing used at all times (not stone inscriptions).
<cite ref="Shabbat 103a:9">Sabb. 103ᵃ</cite> <he>אין דרך כ׳ בכך</he> this (using the left hand) is not the way of writing.

<cite ref="Shabbat 103b:13">Ib.ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <he>וכ̇ת̇ב̇ת̇ם̇</he>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:9">Deut. VI, 9</cite>) <he>שתהא כ̇ת̇יב̇ה ת̇מ̇ה</he> that the writing must be perfect. Ib. 105ᵃ (expl. <he>א̇נ̇כ̇י̇</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 20:2">Ex. XX, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="A02248"><he>אָנֹכִי</he></cite>) <he>א̇מירה נ̇עימה כ̇</he>' <he>י̇היבה</he> a sweet proclamation, a writing, a gift; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 81:7">Yalk. Gen. 81</cite>.
<cite ref="Gittin 17b:7">Gitt. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>משעת כ׳ ועד וכ׳</he> from the time the letter of divorce was written to the time of its delivery.

<cite ref="Gittin 45b:6">Ib. 45ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:8-9">Deut. VI, 8—9</cite>) <he>כל שישנו בקשירה ישנו בכ׳</he> only he who is under the obligation of binding (the T’fillin on his arm), is fit for writing (the scrolls of the Law &c.).
<cite ref="Ketubot 102b:7">Keth. 102ᵇ</cite> <he>וקרי ליה לאמירה כ׳</he> and is ‘saying’ (verbal declaration) called ‘writing’ (consignment)?; a. fr.

<cite ref="Berakhot 16a:4">Ber. 16ᵃ</cite> <he>בין כ׳ לכ׳ וכ׳</he> if a person in reading the Sh’ma is in doubt as to whether he is at <he>וכתבתם</he> (of <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:9">Deut. VI, 9</cite>) or at <he>וכתבתם</he> (of ib. XI, 20), he must go back to the first <he>וכתבתם</he>; Y. ib. II, 5ᵃ <cite ref="K01359"><he>כתיבת</he></cite> (corr. acc.).
